headline: Turin founders who ship agentic AI in public this quarter will own the next funding narrative.
why_now: AI Agents and Agentic Workflows are exploding across GitHub (96) and Hugging Face (92) with news momentum (88) and strong job demand (85) signaling real market pull, not just hype. As a founder in Turin, your edge comes from combining local industry strengths (automotive, manufacturing, fintech) with this global shift toward autonomous, multi-step AI systems. The 96 project_potential score confirms there is a wide-open lane for portfolio work that stands out.
study: Read Anthropic's 'Building Effective Agents' and the LangChain ReAct and LangGraph docs end-to-end in week 1
Clone and run the top 5 agent repos on GitHub filtered by stars in the last 90 days; instrument each with tracing
Complete the DeepLearning.AI 'Agentic Workflows' short course plus the Hugging Face smol-course on tool-using agents
Build a small eval harness using inspect-ai or promptfoo to measure tool-call accuracy and step efficiency
Study 2 Turin-relevant use cases deeply: multilingual customer ops for FCA/Stellantis suppliers and compliance triage for local fintechs

build.title: PiùAgent - a Turin-aware operations copilot
build.description: A multi-agent system that takes a natural-language ops request from a Turin SME (e.g., a supplier to the automotive or fashion-tech cluster), plans the steps, calls real tools (calendar, email, inventory API, web search in Italian), and ships a verifiable action with receipts. It impresses because it is agentic end-to-end, not a chatbot wrapper, and it speaks the local language and respects EU/GDPR constraints.
stack: OpenAI or open-source model via Ollama
deliverables: Public GitHub repo with clean architecture diagram, tests, and CI
Live demo deployed on a Turin-region VPS or Fly.io with a recorded Loom walkthrough
Technical write-up on Hashnode or your blog with eval numbers and cost-per-task
One-page case study PDF in English and Italian aimed at investors and local SMBs

publish: Post a 60-second build-in-public video on LinkedIn and X every Friday for 4 weeks showing one new tool integration
Submit a talk proposal to Turin AI Meetup, Codemotion Italy, and PyData Turin; offer a free hands-on workshop
Publish a thread on X breaking down an open-source agent repo with your own benchmarks, tagging the maintainers
Reach out to 10 Turin-based founders and 5 EU VCs with a personalized Loom and the case-study PDF
skills: Multi-step planning with retrieval and reflection
LLM evaluation, tracing, and cost optimization
FastAPI backend engineering with vector search
EU data privacy and GDPR-aware system design
risks: Vendor lock-in if you over-optimize for one model provider; design with a model-agnostic layer from day one
Eval theater: shipping agents without a real eval harness will not survive technical due diligence from anyone hiring or funding you
Burnout from chasing every new agent framework; pick LangGraph + one open-source model and stick with them for the quarter
confidence: Very high: the signals are strong, the stack is mature, and a Turin-specific agent demo is a credible wedge for both a portfolio and a fundable company.
